claims.text: Stainless steel relies on a native chromium oxide passivation layer for corrosion protection.
The native chromium oxide passivation layer is insufficient in aggressive corrosive environments.
TiN can be deposited on stainless steel by physical vapor deposition using sputtering.
A high-throughput, data-driven machine-learning model can optimize sputtering temperature, power, and film thickness.
Optimized PVD parameters will enable formation of a uniformly dense TiN coating.
Optimized PVD parameters will enable formation of an adherent TiN coating.
The deposited TiN surface layer will be chemically inert under the proposed corrosive conditions.
High-chloride and high-temperature exposures can cause failure of the native stainless-steel passivation layer.
A dense and adherent TiN coating acts as a barrier to corrosive species.
The TiN coating minimizes diffusion of corrosive species to the stainless-steel substrate.
The TiN coating protects the substrate without altering the bulk properties of the stainless steel.
Machine-learning-optimized PVD TiN coating will substantially improve corrosion resistance relative to untreated stainless steel.
The improvement will be observable as a reduced corrosion rate.
The optimized coating will exhibit enhanced durability under severe corrosive conditions.
Protective performance is contingent on precise control of the PVD deposition parameters.
Failure to optimize or maintain the deposition conditions may limit the TiN coating's protective performance.
